title: The Life of JD Vance (English Listening Practice)
speaker: Alastair Budge

sentences.en: Hello, hello, hello, and welcome to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English, the show where you can listen to fascinating stories and learn weird and wonderful things about the world at the same time as improving your English.
sentences.zh: 你好，你好，你好，欢迎收听由 Leonardo English 带来的适合求知者的英语学习播客。在这个节目中，你可以聆听精彩的故事，了解世界上奇妙而有趣的事情，同时提升你的英语水平。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, and today we are going to be talking about the American vice president, JD Vance.
sentences.zh: 我是阿斯泰尔·巴奇（Alastair Budge），今天我们要聊聊美国副总统 JD Vance。

sentences.en: Love him or loathe him, he is important, and by the time you listen to this episode, perhaps he will be even more so.
sentences.zh: 不论你是喜欢他还是讨厌他，他都很重要。等你听到这集节目的时候，也许他会变得更加举足轻重。

sentences.en: So today we will take a look at his life, where he came from, how he says this shaped his political views, and his journey so far almost to the top of American politics.
sentences.zh: 所以今天，我们将探讨他的人生经历：他从哪里来，他是如何看待这些经历对他的政治观点产生影响的，以及他一路走到接近美国政治权力巅峰的历程。

sentences.en: OK then, let's not waste a minute and get right into it.
sentences.zh: 好了，那我们废话少说，马上开始吧。

sentences.en: In 1937, George Orwell published The Road to Wigan Pier.
sentences.zh: 1937年，乔治·奥威尔（George Orwell）出版了《通往威根码头之路》（The Road to Wigan Pier）。

sentences.en: In it, he describes the harsh day-to-day lives of the working class in the North of England.
sentences.zh: 在书中，他描绘了英格兰北部工人阶级严酷的日常生活。

sentences.en: From details about the mechanics of washing clothes right through to the daily struggle to get enough money to feed their families, it shone a light on the bleak reality of life in industrial towns and cities.
sentences.zh: 从洗衣服的具体细节，到为挣够养家糊口的钱而日夜挣扎，这本书揭露了工业城镇里暗淡的生活现实。

sentences.en: To his middle-class readers sipping their tea and sitting on comfortable armchairs, the book pulled back the curtain on a world they knew existed, but understood effectively nothing about.
sentences.zh: 对于那些端着茶杯、坐在舒适扶手椅上的中产阶级读者来说，这本书拉开了帷幕，让他们看到了一个他们知道存在却几乎一无所知的世界。

sentences.en: And in the second half of the book, Orwell turned on his own readers.
sentences.zh: 在书的后半部分，奥威尔将矛头指向了自己的读者。

sentences.en: He argued that the very people most likely to be reading the book — who were educated, comfortable, and said that they supported better social welfare — these were precisely the people who were standing in the way of change.
sentences.zh: 他认为，最有可能读这本书的那些人——受过良好教育、生活舒适、口口声声支持改善社会福利的人——恰恰是阻碍变革发生的人。

sentences.en: It wasn’t because they had bad intentions, but because of something more uncomfortable: they found the working class sort of disgusting, their smell, their manners, their way of life.
sentences.zh: 这倒不是因为他们有什么坏心思，而是因为某种更让人不舒服的原因：他们觉得工人阶级有点恶心，他们的气味、他们的礼貌、他们的生活方式。

sentences.en: Orwell’s readers might claim to support liberal, even socialist policies, but quietly they were physically repulsed by the lives of the people these policies were meant to help.
sentences.zh: 奥威尔的读者或许会声称自己支持自由主义甚至是社会主义政策，但私下里，他们对这些政策本想帮助的人的生活感到生理上的排斥。

sentences.en: His editor suggested Orwell remove the entire second half altogether.
sentences.zh: 他的编辑建议奥威尔把后半部分全部删掉。

sentences.en: Orwell refused. The book became something of a window into a world people said they cared about, that politicians said they represented, but which Orwell contested they had no real understanding of.
sentences.zh: 奥威尔拒绝了。这本书成了一扇窗户，让人得以窥见一个人们口中说在乎、政客口中说代表的世界，但奥威尔坚称，他们对这个世界根本没有真正的理解。

sentences.en: This book, and the idea in the second half of it, well it never really went away.
sentences.zh: 这本书，以及它后半部分的观点，其实从未真正消失过。

sentences.en: Every generation or so, when something happens that makes the comfortable classes realise they understood their country far less than they thought, someone picks it up again.
sentences.zh: 大约每隔一代人，当发生某些事情让舒适的阶层意识到他们对这个国家的理解远比想象中要少时，就会有人重新翻出这本书。

sentences.en: It happened after Margaret Thatcher. It happened after Brexit.
sentences.zh: 玛格丽特·撒切尔（Margaret Thatcher）之后发生过。英国脱欧之后也发生过。

sentences.en: Each time, it serves as a reminder that there are whole worlds within a society that most people simply do not see or understand, especially those in positions of political power.
sentences.zh: 每一次，它都在提醒人们，社会内部存在着许多大多数人根本看不到或不理解的广阔世界，尤其是那些身居政治权力高位的人。

sentences.en: Almost exactly eighty years after the publication of The Road to Wigan Pier, in 2016, on the other side of the Atlantic, another book was published.
sentences.zh: 几乎在《通往威根码头之路》出版整整八十年后的2016年，在大西洋的另一端，另一本书出版了。

sentences.en: It was called Hillbilly Elegy, and was the memoir of a then 31-year-old investment professional called JD Vance.
sentences.zh: 它叫《乡下人的悲歌》（Hillbilly Elegy），是一位当时31岁的投资专业人士 JD Vance 的回忆录。

sentences.en: Now, JD Vance is no Orwell but he does tell quite a good story.
sentences.zh: 如今，JD Vance 算不上奥威尔，但他确实讲了一个相当不错的故事。

sentences.en: And the story was his own: a chaotic childhood, a mother with drug problems, his struggle to break out of a system that seemed to drag so many others down.
sentences.zh: 而这个故事就是他自己的：混乱的童年，有毒瘾的母亲，以及他在一个似乎拖垮了无数人的体系中艰难挣扎并最终突围的故事。

sentences.en: It was also a political commentary on a part of America that he said had been left behind: the Rust Belt, which is the stretch of the northeastern and midwestern United States that was once the industrial heartland, but has been in serious decline.
sentences.zh: 这也是对美国某一部分他所说已被遗忘的地区进行的政治评论：铁锈地带（Rust Belt），也就是美国东北部和中西部曾经的工业核心地带，但目前正处于严重衰落之中。

sentences.en: States like Ohio, Pennsylvania, Michigan, and Indiana.
sentences.zh: 像俄亥俄州、宾夕法尼亚州、密歇根州和印第安纳州这样的地方。

sentences.en: It was also an attempt to explain what had happened to communities like the one he came from.
sentences.zh: 这也是一次试图解释像他出身的那类社区究竟发生了什么变化的尝试。

sentences.en: Why had they struggled so much? Why was violence so endemic?
sentences.zh: 为什么他们的生活如此挣扎？为什么暴力现象如此普遍？

sentences.en: Why had they been particularly devastated by the opioid crisis?
sentences.zh: 为什么他们受阿片类药物危机的影响尤为严重？

sentences.en: Why did so many young men end up in prison or without jobs?
sentences.zh: 为什么那么多年轻男性最终锒铛狱或失业？

sentences.en: This book was published in June 2016, and, as you may remember, this was just as a rather unusual presidential election was reaching its most intense phase.
sentences.zh: 这本书出版于2016年6月，正如你可能记得的那样，当时正值一场相当不寻常的总统大选进入最白热化的阶段。

sentences.en: A year beforehand, Donald Trump had announced his candidacy for the presidency, and he had been winning support in precisely the kind of communities Vance wrote about.
sentences.zh: 前一年，唐纳德·特朗普（Donald Trump）宣布竞选总统，并且一直在 Vace 所写的这类社区中赢得支持。

sentences.en: Trump claimed to understand these communities, but he made no claim to be like them; his entire brand was about wealth and power, New York penthouses and golden chandeliers.
sentences.zh: 特朗普声称自己理解这些社区，但他并没有假装自己和他们是一类人；他的整个标签都建立在财富和权力之上，比如纽约的顶层公寓和金色的枝形吊灯。

sentences.en: Suddenly, journalists and television producers needed someone to explain these communities to the rest of America.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，记者和电视制作人需要有人来向其余的美国人解释这些社区。

sentences.en: JD Vance, with his unusual combination of Yale degree and Rust Belt background, well, he was perfectly placed to do exactly that.
sentences.zh: JD Vance 凭借其耶鲁学位和铁锈地带背景这一不同寻常的结合，被完美地放置在能够做到这一点的绝佳位置上。

sentences.en: Almost overnight, JD Vance became a national figure — someone whose voice was sought out whenever people wanted to understand what was happening in those forgotten corners of America.
sentences.zh: 几乎一夜之间，JD Vance 成了全国知名人物——每当人们想了解美国那些被遗忘的角落正在发生什么时，总会去寻求他的声音。

sentences.en: The publicity turbocharged his book, and it became a massive bestseller.
sentences.zh: 这波宣传让他的书销量暴增，并成为了超级畅销书。

sentences.en: It spent well over a year on the New York Times bestseller list.
sentences.zh: 它在《纽约时报》畅销书排行榜上停留了远超一年的时间。

sentences.en: It was translated into dozens of languages.
sentences.zh: 它被翻译成了几十种语言。

sentences.en: And in 2020, it would get its own film version, directed by Ron Howard.
sentences.zh: 并且在2020年，它被改编成同名电影，由朗·霍华德（Ron Howard）执导。

sentences.en: And then on the 15th of July, 2024, as part of his campaign for re-election, Donald Trump would announce that his running mate and candidate for Vice President would be none other than the then 39-year-old JD Vance.
sentences.zh: 然后在2024年7月15日，作为他竞选连任造势的一部分，唐纳德·特朗普宣布，他的竞选搭档兼副总统候选人正是当时39岁的 JD Vance。

sentences.en: But to understand why Trump chose him, and why the choice made sense to so many Americans, we need to understand where he started.
sentences.zh: 但要理解特朗普为什么选择他，以及为什么这个选择对那么多美国人来说合情合理，我们需要了解他是从哪里开始的。

sentences.en: His name at birth, in August 1984, was James Donald Bowman, and he was born and raised in Middletown, Ohio.
sentences.zh: 他出生于1984年8月，出生时的名字叫詹姆斯·唐纳德·鲍曼（James Donald Bowman），在俄亥俄州米德尔敦（Middletown）出生并长大。

sentences.en: His family background was complicated from the very beginning.
sentences.zh: 他的家庭背景从一开始就很复杂。

sentences.en: His parents divorced when he was still a toddler.
sentences.zh: 在他还是个幼儿时，父母就离婚了。

sentences.en: His father all but disappeared from his life.
sentences.zh: 他的父亲几乎从他的生活中彻底消失了。

sentences.en: His mother struggled deeply with drug addiction, both heroin and prescription opioids.
sentences.zh: 他的母亲饱受毒瘾困扰，既有海洛因，也有处方阿片类药物。

sentences.en: And his early life was unstable, often unhappy, and at times, frightening.
sentences.zh: 他的早期生活动荡不安，常常不快乐，有时甚至令人恐惧。

sentences.en: He writes about this very openly in Hillbilly Elegy.
sentences.zh: 他在《乡下人的悲歌》中非常坦诚地写到了这一点。

sentences.en: He described living through multiple stepfathers, the constant instability, and real fear, sometimes even for his life.
sentences.zh: 他描述了经历多位继父、持续的不稳定以及真正的恐惧，有时甚至担心自己的生命安全。

sentences.en: There’s a particularly memorable scene in the book where his mother is driving with him in the backseat and she threatens to kill them both by crashing the car.
sentences.zh: 书中有个特别让人印象深刻的场景：他的母亲带着坐在后排的他开车，并威胁说要通过撞车来让他们母子俩同归于尽。

sentences.en: But amid all of this chaos, there were two people who provided some stability: his grandparents, Mamaw and Papaw.
sentences.zh: 但在所有这些混乱之中，有两个人为他提供了一些稳定性：他的祖父母，Mamaw 和 Papaw。

sentences.en: Mamaw, in particular, is a figure who appears again and again in everything Vance has written or said about his childhood.
sentences.zh: 尤其是 Mamaw，在 Vance 后来所有关于童年的书写和言论中，这个形象一次又一次地出现。

sentences.en: She was tough, fiercely loyal, deeply religious in her own way, and utterly determined that her grandson would not be swallowed up by the circumstances around him.
sentences.zh: 她性格刚强，极其忠诚，以她自己独特的方式笃信宗教，并且坚决不让自己的孙子被周围的环境吞没。

sentences.en: She made sure he had what he needed to go to school.
sentences.zh: 她确保他有上学所需的东西。

sentences.en: She gave him a place to live when his home life became unbearable.
sentences.zh: 当他的家庭生活变得让人无法忍受时，她为他提供了一个住处。

sentences.en: She pushed him to do things that he wouldn't have done on his own.
sentences.zh: 她督促他去做那些他自己不会主动去做的事情。

sentences.en: And by the time Vance was around fifteen or sixteen years old, he had moved out of his mother's home permanently and was living with his grandmother.
sentences.zh: 到了 Vance 大约十五六岁的时候，他已经彻底搬出了母亲的家，和祖母住在一起。

sentences.en: He graduated from high school in 2003, and rather than going straight to university or trying to get a job, he enlisted in the military as what’s called a “combat correspondent”, essentially a military journalist, someone who follows the troops, takes pictures, and writes articles.
sentences.zh: 他在2003年从高中毕业，但没有直接去上大学或尝试找工作，而是参军成了一名所谓的“战斗记者”（combat correspondent），本质上就是一名军事记者，负责跟随部队、拍照并撰写文章。

sentences.en: He served for four years, including a tour in Iraq.
sentences.zh: 他服役了四年，其中包括一次伊客服役经历。

sentences.en: As he would describe in his memoir, the military gave him something that his childhood had not: structure, discipline, and a sense of belonging.
sentences.zh: 正如他在回忆录中所描述的，军队给予了他童年所不具备的东西：结构、纪律以及归属感。

sentences.en: When he left the military in 2007, he used a government scheme called the GI Bill to study at Ohio State University.
sentences.zh: 2007年退伍后，他利用一项名为《退伍军人权利法案》（GI Bill）的政府资助计划进入俄亥俄州立大学学习。

sentences.en: At school, his grades had been fine, but nothing special.
sentences.zh: 在中学时，他的成绩一直还不错，但也谈不上拔尖。

sentences.en: At college, or at university as we’d say in the UK, something clearly changed.
sentences.zh: 到了大学，或者像我们在英国所说的高等院校，情况显然发生了改变。

sentences.en: He graduated in 2009 with the highest honours, with a degree in political science and philosophy.
sentences.zh: 他在2009年以最高荣誉毕业，获得了政治学和哲学学位。

sentences.en: Now, Ohio State is a well-rated public university, but his next step would be into a world as foreign to him as the world of the Lancashire miners was to a doctor from Bristol: he was accepted into Yale Law School.
sentences.zh: 如今，俄亥俄州立大学是一所评价不错的公立大学，但他接下来的跨越，对于他来说，就像兰开夏郡的矿工对于布里斯托尔的医生一样陌生：他被耶鲁法学院（Yale Law School）录取了。

sentences.en: Yale Law School is not just any university.
sentences.zh: 耶鲁法学院可不仅仅是一所普通的大学。

sentences.en: It's one of the most prestigious universities in the United States, a place where Supreme Court justices, senators, and presidents have passed through.
sentences.zh: 它是美国声望最高的高等学府之一，许多最高法院大法官、参议员和总统都曾在那里求学。

sentences.en: For a kid from small-town Ohio, whose mother had battled addiction and whose childhood had been defined by instability, getting into Yale was, to put it simply, extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 对于一个来自俄亥俄州小镇、母亲饱受毒瘾折磨且童年充满动荡的孩子来说，能进入耶鲁，简单来说，简直非同寻常。

sentences.en: And Vance said that when he first arrived, he felt completely out of place.
sentences.zh: Vance 曾说，他刚到那里时，觉得自已格格不入。

sentences.en: He was surrounded by people who had gone to elite private schools, whose parents were surgeons and lawyers and politicians.
sentences.zh: 周围都是些上过精英私立学校的人，他们的父母是外科医生、律师和政客。

sentences.en: He did not know the unwritten rules. He did not know which fork to use at a formal dinner.
sentences.zh: 他不懂那些不成文的规矩。他不知道在正式晚宴上该用哪把叉子。

sentences.en: He did not speak the language of the professional class in the way his classmates seemed to do effortlessly.
sentences.zh: 他不像同学那样能够不费吹灰之力地说着职业阶层的语言。

sentences.en: But he was smart, he worked hard, and he had something his classmates often lacked: a story.
sentences.zh: 但他很聪明，工作努力，而且他拥有同学们通常不具备的东西：一个故事。

sentences.en: A real, raw, lived experience of a part of America that most of his professors and fellow students had never seen.
sentences.zh: 一个真实的、赤裸裸的、亲身经历过的美国社会切面，而他的大多数教授和同学从未亲眼见过。

sentences.en: At Yale, he met two women who would change his life.
sentences.zh: 在耶鲁，他遇到了两个改变他一生命运的女性。

sentences.en: The first was a fellow student, and the woman who would become his wife, Usha.
sentences.zh: 第一个是他的同学，也就是后来成为他妻子的乌莎（Usha）。

sentences.en: She was the daughter of Indian immigrants and was herself a highly accomplished lawyer.
sentences.zh: 她是印度移民的女儿，本身就是一位极有成就的律师。

sentences.en: The second was a professor named Amy Chua, whose name you might recognise from her book about being a Tiger Mum, and how children benefit from being pushed to study, play musical instruments, and so on.
sentences.zh: 第二个是一位名叫蔡美儿（Amy Chua）的教授，你可能会从她关于“虎妈”的书籍中认出这个名字，书中讲述了孩子们如何从被逼着学习、演奏乐器等方面受益。

sentences.en: Chua had published her book, Battle Hymn of the Tiger Mother, in 2011.
sentences.zh: 蔡美儿于2011年出版了她的书《虎妈战歌》（Battle Hymn of the Tiger Mother）。

sentences.en: It quickly became a bestseller, and had brought the already successful Chua countless opportunities.
sentences.zh: 这本书迅速成为畅销书，并为本已功成名就的蔡美儿带来了无数机遇。

sentences.en: She knew Vance’s backstory, and encouraged him to write about his life.
sentences.zh: 她了解 Vance 的身世背景，并鼓励他把自己的生活写下来。

sentences.en: He did. And the result was Hillbilly Elegy, a book that opened doors Vance didn’t even know existed.
sentences.zh: 他照做了。结果就是《乡下人的悲歌》的诞生，这本书为 Vance 推开了一扇他甚至不知道其存在的通往未知世界的大门。

sentences.en: Now, after graduating from Yale, he spent a few years in the legal world, first working for a district judge, and then at a corporate law firm.
sentences.zh: 从耶鲁毕业后，他在法律界度过了几年，先是为一名地方法官工作，后来又在一家企业律所供职。

sentences.en: But being a lawyer, he soon discovered, wasn’t for him.
sentences.zh: 但很快他发现，做律师并不适合他。

sentences.en: He moved to California and started working in venture capital, investing in technology startups.
sentences.zh: 他搬到加利福尼亚，开始从事风险投资，投资科技初创公司。

sentences.en: He eventually ended up working for a firm backed by Peter Thiel, the billionaire tech investor, who became something of a mentor to Vance.
sentences.zh: 最终，他进入了一家由亿万富翁科技投资者彼得·蒂尔（Peter Thiel）支持的公司工作，蒂尔后来成了 Vance 的良师益友。

sentences.en: Now, Thiel is a fascinating and controversial figure.
sentences.zh: 如今，蒂尔是一个迷人且备受争议的人物。

sentences.en: He was one of the founders of PayPal, an early investor in Facebook, and has accumulated enormous wealth and political influence.
sentences.zh: 他是 PayPal 的创始人之一，是 Facebook 的早期投资者，积累了巨大的财富和政治影响力。

sentences.en: He is also someone who has been quite open about his desire to reshape American politics in a more nationalist, anti-establishment direction.
sentences.zh: 同时，他也毫不掩饰自己希望按照更具民族主义、反建制的方向重塑美国政治的愿望。

sentences.en: When Vance launched his political career, Thiel provided much of the financial backing.
sentences.zh: 当 Vance 开启自己的政治生涯时，蒂尔提供了大量的资金支持。

sentences.en: Vance was working for Thiel when he published his bestselling memoir.
sentences.zh: Vance 出版畅销回忆录时，正是在为蒂尔工作。

sentences.en: For Vance's critics, this raises an obvious question.
sentences.zh: 在 Vance 的批评者看来，这引发了一个显而易见的问题。

sentences.en: Here is a man who presents himself as the champion of forgotten, working-class Americans, and yet his political career and success were largely bankrolled by one of the wealthiest and most powerful figures in Silicon Valley.
sentences.zh: 这是一个把自己包装成被遗忘的美国工人阶级斗士的人，然而他的政治生涯和成功却在很大程度上由硅谷最富有、最有权势的人物之一资助。

sentences.en: The very world, in other words, that Vance himself has described as a self-serving elite.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，也就是 Vance 本人曾形容为自私自利的精英阶层。

sentences.en: Whether that is a damning contradiction or simply the reality of how American politics is funded, well, that’s something you can make up your own mind about.
sentences.zh: 不管这算是一个致命的矛盾，还是仅仅体现了美国政治资金来源的现实，好吧，你可以自己下定论。

sentences.en: Now, to understand how the political career began, we need to go back briefly to the book, and what happened in its aftermath.
sentences.zh: 为了理解这段政治生涯是如何开始的，我们需要简要回顾一下那本书，以及它出版之后发生的事情。

sentences.en: We've already talked about the book's extraordinary timing and its immediate impact, in terms of Vance being called upon as the authoritative source on understanding the working class America.
sentences.zh: 我们已经谈到过这本书非凡的出版时机以及它带来的即时影响，即 Vance 被推崇为理解美国工人阶级的权威信源。

sentences.en: But there is something else worth understanding about what happened to Vance in the years that followed its publication.
sentences.zh: 但关于 Vance 在书出版后几年的遭遇，还有另一件事情值得了解。

sentences.en: For a time, he occupied a curious position.
sentences.zh: 有一段时间，他占据了一个奇特的位置。

sentences.en: He was famous for understanding Trump voters.
sentences.zh: 他因“懂特朗普选民”而闻名。

sentences.en: He was the man editors and television producers called when they needed someone to explain them: to give them a human face, to make them understandable to a coastal, affluent audience.
sentences.zh: 当编辑和电视制作人需要有人来解释这群人时，他们就会找他：给他们一个具体的人形面孔，让他们能够被沿海富裕阶层的受众所理解。

sentences.en: But privately, JD Vance found Trump reprehensible.
sentences.zh: 但在私下里，JD Vance 觉得特朗普极其令人反感。

sentences.en: In messages that later became public, he called Trump a morally reprehensible human being, and said he went back and forth between thinking, and I’m quoting directly: “Trump is a cynical a--hole like Nixon who wouldn't be that bad [and might even prove useful] or that he's America's Hitler.”
sentences.zh: 在后来被公之于众的短信中，他称特朗普是一个道德上令人作呕的人，并说他在以下两种想法之间摇摆不定——我直接引用原话：“特朗普就像尼克松那样是个愤世嫉俗的混蛋，其实也没那么糟（甚至可能证明有用）”或者“他是美国的希特勒”。

sentences.en: He did not vote for Trump in 2016, and was a public “Never Trumper”.
sentences.zh: 他在2016年没有投票给特朗普，曾是一个公开的“反特朗普派”（Never Trumper）。

sentences.en: But sometime during Trump’s first term, he changed his tune.
sentences.zh: 但在特朗普第一个任期的某个时候，他改变了调门。

sentences.en: When Vance announced in 2021 that he was running for a seat in the United States Senate, representing Ohio, he ran as a strong Trump supporter.
sentences.zh: 当 Vance 在2021年宣布竞选代表俄亥俄州的美国参议院席位时，他是作为特朗普的坚定支持者参选的。

sentences.en: He publicly apologised for his earlier criticisms, deleted social media posts in which he had attacked Trump, and asked for Trump's endorsement.
sentences.zh: 他公开为自己早期的批评道歉，删除了曾攻击特朗普的社交媒体帖子，并请求特朗普的背书支持。

sentences.en: Trump gave it. And with that endorsement, Vance won the Republican primary in Ohio and then the Senate seat itself in November 2022.
sentences.zh: 特朗普支持了他。凭借这份背书，Vance 赢得了俄亥俄州的共和党初选，并在2022年11月赢得了参议员席位。

sentences.en: His critics say this transformation tells you everything you need to know about his character, that he is a deeply opportunistic politician who will say whatever is necessary to advance his career.
sentences.zh: 他的批评者说，这种转变说明了他的一切本质，证明他是一个极度投机的政客，为了推进自己的政治前途会说任何必要的话。

sentences.en: His supporters say that people are allowed to change their minds, that Vance genuinely came to believe that Trump's instincts about the working class were correct, and that the transformation represents an honest evolution of his thinking.
sentences.zh: 他的支持者说，人是允许改变看法的，Vance 是真心开始相信特朗普对工人阶级的直觉是正确的，这种转变代表了他思想上的一次真诚演变。

sentences.en: I’ll leave that without comment, but what is certainly true is that without Trump's endorsement, Vance would almost certainly not have won the primary.
sentences.zh: 我就对此不予置评了，但可以肯定的是，如果没有特朗普的背书，Vance 几乎不可能赢得初选。

sentences.en: The working-class champion needed the billionaire's blessing to get through the door.
sentences.zh: 这位工人阶级的斗士需要亿万富翁的祝福才能敲开这扇大门。

sentences.en: And as a senator, Vance quickly established himself as one of the most prominent voices of what is sometimes called America First conservatism, or national conservatism.
sentences.zh: 作为一名参议员，Vance 迅速确立了自己的地位，成为有时被称为“美国优先保守主义”（America First conservatism）或民族保守主义的最杰出声音之一。

sentences.en: So, what does that mean in practice? Well, the overarching theme is, as the term suggests, to put American interests first, both at home and abroad.
sentences.zh: 那么，这在实践中意味着什么呢？好吧，顾名思义，其核心主题就是将美国利益放在首位，无论是在国内还是国外。

sentences.en: On foreign policy, Vance has been consistent in arguing that the United States spends too much money and political energy on foreign conflicts — particularly in Europe and the Middle East — when it should be focusing on problems at home.
sentences.zh: 在外交政策上，Vance 一贯主张美国在海外冲突——特别是在欧洲和中东——花费了太多的金钱和政治精力，而本应把重点放在解决国内问题上。

sentences.en: He has been one of the most prominent sceptics of American aid to Ukraine, and has argued that Europe needs to take far greater responsibility for its own defence rather than relying on American support.
sentences.zh: 他是对美国援助乌克兰持最强烈怀疑态度的人之一，并主张欧洲需要承担起更多自身防务的责任，而不是依赖美国的支援。

sentences.en: On the economy, he positions himself as someone who speaks on behalf of ordinary working people against what he sees as a self-serving elite class of politicians, journalists, and business leaders.
sentences.zh: 在经济上，他把自己定位为普通劳动人民的代言人，对抗他眼中自私自利的政客、记者和商界领袖等精英阶层。

sentences.en: He has been more willing than many traditional conservatives to support measures that protect American manufacturing, even when those conflict with the free trade principles his party has historically championed.
sentences.zh: 与许多传统保守派相比，他更愿意支持保护美国制造业的措施，即使这些措施与他所在政党一贯倡导的自由贸易原则相冲突。

sentences.en: On social issues, he is very conservative.
sentences.zh: 在社会问题上，他是极度保守的。

sentences.en: He is anti-abortion, and has spoken extensively about the importance of what he calls family formation, and the danger of falling birth rates in America.
sentences.zh: 他反堕胎，并广泛谈论他所谓的“家庭组建”（family formation）的重要性，以及美国出生率下降的危机。

sentences.en: Essentially he is all about encouraging people to get married and have children.
sentences.zh: 本质上，他的一切主张都是为了鼓励人们结婚生子。

sentences.en: On immigration, he has taken a very strict position, supporting tight restrictions on both legal and illegal immigration.
sentences.zh: 在移民问题上，他采取了非常强硬的立场，支持对合法移民和非法移民都实施严格限制。

sentences.en: And on matters of culture and free expression, he has been increasingly critical of what he sees as the suppression of conservative voices, both in the United States and in Europe.
sentences.zh: 在文化和言论自由问题上，他越来越批评他眼中对美国和欧洲保守派声音的压制。

sentences.en: You might remember his speech at the Munich Security Conference in 2025, where rather than reassuring European allies, he spent his time warning them that the real threat to their continent came not from Russia or China, but from their own leaders.
sentences.zh: 你可能还记得他在2025年慕尼黑安全会议上的演讲，当时他没有去安抚欧洲盟友，而是花时间警告他们，其大陆面临的真正威胁不是来自俄罗斯或中国，而是来自他们自己的领导人。

sentences.en: Now, we’re not going to make this episode too much about the politics of JD Vance, and what he has and hasn’t done since becoming Vice President.
sentences.zh: 好了，我们不会让这集节目过多地纠缠于 JD Vance 的政治立场，以及他在成为副总统之后做了什么或没做什么。

sentences.en: That’s something of an impossible task, and no doubt by the time you listen to this, something new and unpredictable will have happened.
sentences.zh: 那基本上是一个不可能完成的任务，毫无疑问，等你听到这集的时候，肯定已经发生了新鲜且不可预测的事情。

sentences.en: Instead, we are going to look forward, to the future.
sentences.zh: 相反，我们将把目光投向未来。

sentences.en: Donald Trump, under the American Constitution, cannot serve more than two terms as President.
sentences.zh: 根据美国宪法，唐纳德·特朗普担任总统不能超过两届。

sentences.en: His second term began in January 2025 and will end in January 2029.
sentences.zh: 他的第二任期始于2025年1月，将于2029年1月结束。

sentences.en: After that, he cannot run again. This means that the 2028 presidential election will be an open contest for the Republican Party.
sentences.zh: 在此之后，他不能再次参选。这意味着2028年的总统大选将是共和党内部的一场开放式竞争。

sentences.en: And as of early 2026, JD Vance is widely seen as the most likely Republican candidate.
sentences.zh: 截至2026年初，JD Vance 被普遍视为最有可能代表共和党参选的候选人。

sentences.en: The most recent polls have him with a 45% chance of becoming the Republican nominee, with Donald Trump Jr trailing behind at 17%.
sentences.zh: 最近的民调显示，他有45%的概率成为共和党总统候选人，而小唐纳德·特朗普（Donald Trump Jr）以17%的支持率紧随其后。

sentences.en: Clearly, a lot can change and no doubt will change between now and November 2028, but were Vance to be nominated, and were he to win, he would become the President of the United States at the age of just 44, making him one of the youngest presidents in US history.
sentences.zh: 显然，从现在到2028年11月之间，很多事情可能会也毫无疑问会发生变化，但如果 Vance 获得提名并赢得大选，他在44岁时就将成为美国总统，这使他成为美国历史上最年轻的总统之一。

sentences.en: So, to bring us back to where we started.
sentences.zh: 因此，让我们回到最初的话题。

sentences.en: George Orwell's great question — the one his editor wanted to cut, the one that made The Road to Wigan Pier uncomfortable to its readers — was whether the people who claimed to speak for the working class actually understood them.
sentences.zh: 乔治·奥威尔提出的伟大问题——那个他的编辑想要删掉的、让《通往威根码头之路》的读者感到坐立不安的问题——是那些声称代表工人阶级说话的人是否真正理解他们。

sentences.en: Whether they had earned that right. Whether their sympathy was real, or whether it was something more convenient and more self-serving.
sentences.zh: 他们是否赢得了这种权利。他们的同情心是真实的，还是仅仅出于某种更方便、更自私的考量。

sentences.en: A similar question can certainly be asked of JD Vance.
sentences.zh: 同样的问题当然也可以抛给 JD Vance。

sentences.en: He grew up in Middletown. He knows what a community looks like when the jobs disappear and don't come back.
sentences.zh: 他在米德尔敦长大。当工作岗位消失且不再复返时，社区是什么样子，他心知肚明。

sentences.en: But he also went to Yale, worked for Peter Thiel, and is now one of the most powerful people in the world.
sentences.zh: 但他也上过耶鲁，为彼得·蒂尔工作过，如今更是世界上最有权势的人之一。

sentences.en: His supporters see that journey, from a chaotic childhood in small-town Ohio to the second-highest office in the land, they see this as proof that the American dream is still real, and exists in a man who will support and champion them in a way that the coastal elites never will.
sentences.zh: 他的支持者看到这段从俄亥俄州小镇的混乱童年到登上国家第二高权力宝座的旅程，将其视为美国梦依然真实的证明，并认为他会以沿海精英永远不会做到的方式支持和捍卫他们。

sentences.en: His critics see the same journey and ask other questions: was the Trump reversal an honest change of heart, or a calculated political move?
sentences.zh: 他的批评者看到同样的旅程，则提出了其他问题：对特朗普的态度大反转是真诚的幡然醒悟，还是一场精心算计的政治棋局？

sentences.en: And can a man whose career was funded by one of Silicon Valley's wealthiest investors really be the champion of forgotten America?
sentences.zh: 一个职业生涯由硅谷最富有的投资者资助的人，真的能成为被遗忘的美国的斗士吗？

sentences.en: These are not questions with easy answers.
sentences.zh: 这些都不是容易回答的问题。

sentences.en: And whatever you make of him, the story of JD Vance is still being written.
sentences.zh: 无论你对他作何评价，JD Vance 的故事仍在继续书写之中。

sentences.en: OK then. That is it for today's episode on JD Vance — the man from Middletown, Ohio, who might one day be the most powerful person on earth.
sentences.zh: 好了。这就是今天关于 JD Vance 节目的全部内容——这位来自俄亥俄州米德尔敦的男子，有朝一日可能会成为地球上最有权势的人。

sentences.en: As always, I would love to know what you thought of this episode.
sentences.zh: 和往常一样，我很想知道你对这期节目的看法。

sentences.en: What do you think about JD Vance? And what do you think his story tells us?
sentences.zh: 你如何看待 JD Vance？你认为他的故事向我们说明了什么？

sentences.en: You can head right into our community forum, which is at community.leonardoenglish.com and get chatting away to other curious minds.
sentences.zh: 你可以直接登录我们的社区论坛，网址是 community.leonardoenglish.com，与其他求知者畅所欲言。

sentences.en: You've been listening to English Learning for Curious Minds by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 你收听的是由 Leonardo English 带来的适合求知者的英语学习播客。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, you stay safe, and I'll catch you in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 我是阿斯泰尔·巴奇，请注意安全，我们下期节目再见。
